title: The ally of their freedom
line: One relationship, one question: am I the ally of their freedom?
intro: “To love”, Athena says, “means I am the ally of your freedom.” What works against another’s freedom, even quietly (“you will do what I want”), is control, not love. This week you take one relationship, ask the question honestly, and then do one thing on the side of the other’s freedom.
does: Watch one relationship for control, then do one thing for the other’s freedom.
trains: Love as alliance with another’s freedom, not possession.
steps: Choose one person you love: a partner, a child, a parent, a friend.

For a day or two, watch how you are with them. Notice each “you will do what I want”, spoken or silent: advice they did not ask for, a sulk when they choose differently, a plan made for them. Call it by its name: control.
Ask yourself what this person wants to become, or to be free to do. Then do one concrete thing that helps it, as far as you can, without asking anything back.
report: Where did you find control dressed as love?
What did you do for their freedom, and what happened?
